text:
Wake County
Wake County detention officer charged with smuggling drugs into jail
[Key Takeaways]
AI-generated summary reviewed by our newsroom.
- Wake County detention officer arrested for smuggling drugs to inmates.
- Charges include cocaine, synthetic marijuana, Suboxone and conspiracy counts.
- Officer no longer employed; sheriff vows continued accountability measures.
A former Wake County detention officer is accused of smuggling drugs into the downtown Raleigh detention facility.
Hillary Seekins, 31, was arrested during her shift inside the John H. Baker Jr. Public Safety Center on Wednesday morning, according to a Wake County Sheriff’s Office news release.
She is charged with possession with intent to manufacture, sell or deliver cocaine, K2 or synthetic marijuana and suboxone, a schedule III prescription medicine used to treat opioid use; possession of a controlled substance in jail; and three counts of conspiracy of possession with the intent to manufacture, sell or deliver a controlled substance.
“As soon as these allegations were reported, we took immediate action and launched an investigation,” according to Sheriff Willie Rowe in a news release.
“We will not tolerate any conduct that compromises the safety of our community or the integrity of this agency,” he said.
Seekins, who as of Wednesday no longer works for the Sheriff’s Office, was placed under $50,000 unsecured bail.
The Sheriff’s Office declined to say when and how it learned about the allegations.
This story was originally published September 3, 2025 at 4:29 PM.
